correctness.rationale: The orbit criterion is exact: an orbit O_theta exists iff 2 min(theta, pi-theta) < r. For r <= 2pi/3, low and high orbit cells cannot share a simplex because both cross-distances exceed pi-r/2 >= r; each orbit attaches to one of the two fixed vertices, so the fixed locus has exactly two components. For 2pi/3 < r <= pi, explicit theta and phi in nonempty open intervals produce a simplex joining the two components. For r > pi the Rips complex is a full simplex. Equality is handled by strict inequalities. The fixed-endpoint path obstruction gives the stated infinite-TC corollary on the disconnected side.
